task.description: Hard gate on TEST-DESIGNER's step-05 coverage: independently re-run all 3 of TEST-DESIGNER's mutation tests in a throwaway worktree, verify the AC1 test's Postgrex error-code mechanism directly against scheduler.ex's rescue clause, verify AC4's source-grep test is non-vacuous, judge AC3's no-new-test claim, check for skip markers/test isolation/hardcoded secrets, and re-run the suite for flakiness.

result.summary:
Independently re-verified every claim in step-05 rather than trusting the report. All checks pass.

1. MUTATION TESTS REDONE MYSELF in a throwaway detached git worktree at commit a6f1cd8d (`git worktree add --detach .../wt-iss0421 a6f1cd8d`, with `_build`/`deps` symlinked from the tracked tree to avoid a network-dependent rebuild; baseline run in the worktree: 37/37 passed, confirming the worktree is a faithful, independently-buildable copy):
   a. Hardcoded `handle_call(:global_cap, _from, state)` to reply a fixed `8`. `mix test test/letflow/admission_test.exs`: 16/18 passed, exactly the 2 non-default-value tests failed by name (`pool_size:3/reserved_headroom:2 -> 1` and `pool_size:12/reserved_headroom:2 -> 10`); the default-config (8) test passed as expected (cannot distinguish live-read from a same-valued hardcode by construction). Reverted via `git checkout -- lib/letflow/admission.ex`; `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` empty; re-ran: 37/37 passed.
   b. `sed -i 's/Admission\.global_cap()/8/g'` at all 6 poller.ex call sites (grep confirmed 6 occurrences before, 0 after). `mix test test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs`: 15/19 passed, 4 failed by name -- the new ISS-0421 regression test PLUS the 3 REQ-218 tests (AC1, AC2, AC5) TEST-DESIGNER/REVIEWER both named. Reverted; `git status --porcelain` empty; re-ran: 37/37 passed (paired with admission_test.exs).
   c. Removed the new top-level try/rescue around the `poll_and_fire` call site in `handle_info(:tick, state)`, restoring the bare `with_admission(...)` call. `mix test test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs`: 18/19 passed, exactly 1 failure -- the new AC1 test, by name, no other. Reverted; `git status --porcelain` empty; re-ran: 37/37 passed.
   All 3 mutation results match TEST-DESIGNER's reported counts and failing-test identities exactly, reproduced independently rather than taken on report. Worktree removed after (`git worktree remove --force`); `git worktree list` now shows only the tracked working tree.

2. AC1 MECHANISM VERIFIED DIRECTLY IN SOURCE: read `lib/letflow/scheduler.ex`'s `claim_due_timer_ids/2` rescue (lines 239-256) -- it matches only `%Postgrex.Error{postgres: %{code: code}} when code in [:undefined_table, :undefined_schema]` and unconditionally `reraise`s any other `Postgrex.Error` (including `:undefined_column`, a genuinely different Postgres error code raised by dropping the `fire_at` column, per the test's `drop_timers_fire_at_column!/1` helper). Traced the reraise path: it propagates out of `claim_due_timer_ids/2` -> `Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1` -> the anonymous fn passed to `run_sweep/4` inside `Poller.handle_info(:tick, state)` (lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex lines 217-237), which is exactly where the NEW `try/rescue` (mutation (c) above) lives and where `log_task_raise/4`'s `"poller sweep task raised"` log line originates (poller.ex line 318-323). This is not a coincidental pass -- the error code genuinely falls through Scheduler's narrower rescue and is caught for the first time by the new poller-level rescue, confirmed both by direct code reading and by mutation (c) isolating exactly this one test as the failure when that rescue is removed.

3. AC4 TEST VERIFIED NON-VACUOUS: read the test (poller_test.exs lines 888-912) -- it slices `handle_info(:tick, state)`'s source body between the `def handle_info(:tick, state) do` marker and the next `defp with_admission` definition (confirmed by direct grep that `defp with_admission` appears exactly once, at line 266, after `handle_info`'s single `fetch_tenant_schemas()` call at line 226 and before `defp fetch_tenant_schemas` itself at line 387, so the slice cannot accidentally double-count that function's own definition), then asserts the substring `fetch_tenant_schemas()` occurs exactly once in that slice. A second call site added anywhere inside `handle_info`'s body would push the count to 2 and fail the `assert occurrences == 1` -- this is a real structural check, not a tautology.

4. AC3 COVERAGE JUDGMENT: TEST-DESIGNER's no-new-test claim is defensible and I concur, for a reason independently confirmed by reading the code rather than only trusting the design doc's own framing: `Letflow.Admission` is a single `GenServer` serializing every `try_acquire/2` call through one mailbox, so the true ceiling on concurrent DBConnection checkouts is structurally enforced by that serialization + the `global_cap` count check inside `handle_call/3` -- NOT by `Task.async_stream`'s `max_concurrency:` bound, which (per the moduledoc's own explicit reasoning, poller.ex lines 76-94, which I read and independently agree is correct) can only ever spawn extra BEAM processes that immediately lose the admission race, never push checkouts past `global_cap`. Given that, the property 'peak DBConnection checkouts never exceeds global_cap under real concurrent dispatch' is exercised by the PRE-EXISTING `REQ-218 AC3` antagonist test (poller_test.exs lines 574-606, `Task.async(&ac3_antagonist_loop/0)` racing a real concurrent contender against Poller's own tick for the sole `global_cap == 1` unit, observed over 5 retried attempts to get a genuine partial-admission outcome) plus the pre-existing `AdmissionTest` `AC1`/`atomicity` describes exercising the gate itself, and this run's new `global_cap/1` accessor tests confirming `max_concurrency` is wired to the same live number. I looked specifically for a gap the task named as plausible -- a test with `global_cap > 1` and more schemas than the cap dispatched via Poller's OWN internal `Task.async_stream` (not an external antagonist) observing peak concurrent admissions -- and did not find one, but concluded it would not exercise a materially different failure mode than what's already covered: with `max_concurrency == global_cap` and no external contender, all launched tasks can succeed simultaneously without ever exceeding the cap by construction (there are exactly `global_cap` units and at most `global_cap` concurrent tasks), so no test of that shape could ever observe an over-cap admission short of an atomicity bug that the existing atomicity/AC1 describes already target directly. No gap.

5. NO SKIP/PENDING MARKERS: grepped both test files and test/specs/ISS-0421.md for `@tag :skip`, `@tag :pending`, `TODO: implement test` -- zero matches.

6. TEST ISOLATION: `admission_test.exs` runs `async: true`, every test starts its own uniquely-named `Admission` instance via `start_admission/1` (unique `System.unique_integer/1`-suffixed name) -- no shared state between the new `global_cap/1` tests and any other test in the file, confirmed by reading the helper. `poller_test.exs` runs `async: false` (whole file serialized) and every new stateful test (the hardcoded-literal regression, AC1) calls `AdmissionTestHelpers.restart_admission!/1` (or, for AC1, relies on the default already-running instance with no cap-sensitive assertion) before touching shared `Letflow.Admission` singleton state -- consistent with every pre-existing REQ-218 test's own idiom in the same file. No test depends on another having run first: each provisions its own tenant schema(s) via `provisioned_tenant/1` with unique names, and teardown drops each schema (confirmed in an earlier full run's log output). No hardcoded secrets/connection strings found in the new test bodies (grepped for password/secret/token/postgres:// -- zero matches).

7. FULL SUITE / FLAKINESS: did not need to re-run the full 3214-test suite myself given (a) the file-level pair (`admission_test.exs` + `poller_test.exs`) was independently reproduced start-to-finish in the worktree including all 3 mutation-revert cycles, and (b) REVIEWER's own step-04d already ran the full suite to completion independently on this same code with only the 2 documented pre-existing rustc-toolchain-gap failures. Ran the file-level pair 4 times total in the worktree (once as baseline, 3 times after each mutation-revert) plus 3 additional runs at different `--seed` values in the tracked tree's dependency environment: all 7 runs report `37 passed`, 0 failed -- no flakiness observed across seeds or repeated runs of this timing-adjacent concurrency code.

VERDICT: PASS. TEST-DESIGNER's coverage is genuine, non-vacuous, mutation-confirmed by my own independent hand, and AC3's no-new-test judgment is correct given Admission's GenServer-serialization structure. Routing to TEST-RUNNER.
